scope: CNS pharmacology for Level 3 Clinical Pharmacy students in Egypt (Pharmacology 2 sections): mechanisms, drug classes, therapeutic choice, safety and case realism.
criteria: Mechanisms name the receptor, transporter or enzyme and link it to the clinical effect and the adverse effects.
Each chapter covers every drug class with its prototype and main members.
First-line therapy follows current guidelines (e.g. NICE, APA, ILAE) and is distinguished from alternatives.
Adverse effects, black-box warnings, contraindications and major interactions are complete.
Toxicity and overdose management is given where clinically relevant (e.g. benzodiazepines, local anaesthetics).
Doses, if given, are correct adult doses in standard units.
Comparison tables are accurate and help the student choose between drugs.
Cases are realistic Egyptian practice scenarios that require a decision.
MCQ distractors are plausible; rationales explain the mechanism.
exclusions: Chemical structures and structure-activity relationships are out of scope (user).
Cough and asthma are out of scope (CNS only).
evidence_expectations: Quote the exact text and give file and line for every finding.
Give replacement text, not only a critique.
Cite a standard textbook edition or a current guideline for any correction.
